verse.text: Since, then, you have been raised with Christ, set your hearts on things above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God.

reflection.scripture: Since, then, you have been raised with Christ, set your hearts on things above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God.
reflection.observation: Paul reminds the Colossian believers that their identity has fundamentally changed — they have been 'raised with Christ.' This isn't a future hope alone; it's a present reality. Because of this new life, their focus should shift upward, toward heavenly things, where Christ now reigns. The imagery of Christ seated at God's right hand speaks of completed authority and finished work.
reflection.application: What am I setting my heart on today? It's easy to get consumed by earthly concerns — deadlines, worries, notifications, to-do lists. This verse invites a daily recalibration: lift my gaze, realign my priorities, and let my decisions flow from the truth that I'm already living in Christ's resurrection life. One practical step: before checking my phone in the morning, spend 60 seconds in quiet prayer, setting my heart on 'things above.'
reflection.prayer: Lord, thank You that I have been raised with Christ and my life is hidden in You. Help me lift my eyes above the noise and distractions of this day. Teach me to set my heart on what truly matters — Your kingdom, Your purposes, Your presence. Let my thoughts, my plans, and my interactions today be shaped by the reality that You reign. In Jesus' name, Amen.
